classes.name: Noun
classes.say: A noun is a name for something.
classes.what: A noun is a name: for a person, an animal, a thing or an idea.
classes.tip: Every French noun is masculine or feminine: le livre, la maison. Before a vowel the article doesn't show it (l'école is feminine, l'hôtel masculine), so learn the noun with un or une. Names of people and places start with a capital letter: Inès, Marseille.

learn.label: Nouns and gender: rule and exercises

tr.en: A noun is a name: for a person, an animal, a thing or an idea.

classes.name: Article
classes.also: le, la, l', les, un, une
classes.say: An article comes before a noun.
classes.what: An article comes before a noun and agrees with it: le, la, l', les for a thing we both know; un, une, des for one of many, or some; du, de la for an amount of something.
classes.ask: le or la? un or une?
classes.tip: The article shows the gender and the number: le livre, la maison, les livres. Before a vowel or a silent h, le and la become l': l'ami, l'heure. à + le becomes au and de + le becomes du: je vais au marché, je viens du marché.

learn.label: Articles: le, la, l', les, un, une – rule and exercises

tr.en: An article comes before a noun and agrees with it: le, la, l', les for a thing we both know; un, une, des for one of many, or some; du, de la for an amount of something.

classes.name: Verb
classes.say: A verb says what someone does.

sub.name: pronominal verb
sub.what: A verb that comes with a pronoun: je me lève, tu te souviens, il s'en va.

classes.what: A verb says what someone does or what happens.
classes.ask: What does he do? What happens?
classes.tip: French always needs the subject: je parle, tu parles, il parle. In speech these sound the same, so the pronoun does the work. Infinitives end in -er, -ir or -re: parler, finir, vendre.

tr.en: A verb says what someone does or what happens.

classes.name: Adjective
classes.say: An adjective says what something is like.
classes.what: An adjective says what someone or something is like.
classes.tip: An adjective agrees with its noun and usually goes after it: une maison blanche, des voitures blanches. A few short, common ones go before it: un petit appartement, une belle journée. Adjectives ending in -e are the same for both genders: un appartement calme, une rue calme.

tr.en: An adjective says what someone or something is like.

classes.name: Adverb
classes.say: An adverb says when, where or how.
classes.what: An adverb says when, where or how something happens.
classes.tip: Adverbs don't change their form. Many end in -ment: rapidement, normalement. Others don't: aujourd'hui, ici, toujours, bien.

tr.en: An adverb says when, where or how something happens.

classes.name: Pronoun
classes.say: A pronoun stands for a noun.
classes.what: A pronoun stands for a noun, so you don't have to repeat it.
classes.tip: Léa arrive en retard. → Elle arrive en retard. Je vois Léa. → Je la vois. Object pronouns go before the verb.

tr.en: A pronoun stands for a noun, so you don't have to repeat it.

classes.name: Preposition
classes.say: A preposition comes before a noun: à, en, de.
classes.what: A preposition comes before a noun and shows place, time or direction.
classes.tip: After a preposition, use a noun, a stressed pronoun or an infinitive: avec mon ami, pour toi, avant de partir. à and de join with le and les: au, aux, du, des.

learn.label: Places: à, en, au, aux, chez

tr.en: A preposition comes before a noun and shows place, time or direction.

classes.name: Conjunction
classes.say: A conjunction joins words and sentences.
classes.what: A conjunction joins words or sentences.
classes.tip: et, ou and mais join two sentences: Je suis fatigué, mais je viens. parce que gives a reason. que becomes qu' before a vowel: parce qu'il pleut.

learn.label: et, ou, mais, parce que: rule and exercises

tr.en: A conjunction joins words or sentences.

classes.name: Number
classes.what: A number word says how much or how many, or in which position.
classes.ask: How many? How much? Which one in order?
classes.tip: deux enfants (how many?), le deuxième jour (which one in order?). un becomes une before a feminine noun: un livre, une heure, vingt et une pages.

tr.en: A number word says how much or how many, or in which position.

classes.name: Phrase
classes.also: not a part of speech, a fixed group of words
classes.say: A phrase: several words, one meaning.
classes.what: A phrase is several words that together have one fixed meaning.
classes.tip: Learn it as a whole. Translated word for word, it often doesn't work: Ça va ?

tr.en: A phrase is several words that together have one fixed meaning.
